title: Reading Web Pages Aloud with a Computer
author: Zhiyu
excerpt: Living beings in the Sahā world have the keenest ear faculty. Listening while reading is often easier to understand and remember than reading alone. Therefore, you can use a computer to read the teaching materials aloud while you listen and read along. Moreover, you can steep yourself in the teachings through repeated listening.

Therefore, you can use a computer to read the teaching materials aloud while you listen and read along. Moreover, you can steep yourself in the teachings through repeated listening.

Text-to-speech software is a tool that helps us study. Like any other tool, the more you use it, the more skilled you become, the more noticeable the results, and the better you can put it to good use. For certain words or phrases, if the voice's pronunciation is unsatisfactory, you can use the “escape characters” function to set the pronunciation. For example, for “hùliánwǎng (the Internet)
, the voice will usually read only “hùliánwǎng,” while the “

Another example: “bōrě” (prajñā) would be read with the sound “bānruò,” and “xíng zhù zuò wò” (walking, standing, sitting, and lying down) would be read with the sound “háng zhù zuò wò.” So you can use the “escape characters” page to set up replacements so that they are read with the correct sounds “bōruò” and “xíng zhù zuò wò.”
If you like the content being read to be displayed on the desktop sentence by sentence, like watching a video, click “Read” on the “Langdunü” menu, then click “open
close desktop subtitles.” (If you later want to close the desktop subtitles, just do the same thing again.)
When the mouse points at the desktop subtitles, a toolbar for setting the subtitles will appear; from it you can set the color and font of the subtitles, and choose kara
e mode, as well as close the subtitles.
